content.title: About
content.content: The Quarter Pounder with Cheese is a signature McDonald's burger consisting of a 113 g beef patty, American cheese, pickles, onions, mustard and ketchup, all served on a sesame seed bun.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The burger was introduced to the U.S. menu in 1971 as part of the "Quarter Pounder" line.
In Russia the name "Quarter Pounder with Cheese" has been used officially since 1998.
The cheese is a processed American cheese that melts at about 70 °C.
The patty is cooked on a grill, giving it a distinctive smoky flavor.
In some countries the burger is offered with bacon or BBQ sauce, but the classic version remains unchanged.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The beef patty provides roughly 20 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is highly bioavailable.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: The processed cheese adds a modest amount of calcium for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and cheese supply niacin, vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: At about 530 kcal, the burger provides a quick source of energy, useful for high‑intensity activity.

items.title: High calorie and fat content
items.content: One burger contains roughly 530 kcal and over 30 g of fat, including saturated fats.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Ketchup and pickles add significant salt, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Processed cheese can trigger reactions in individuals allergic to dairy.

items.title: Gluten in the bun
items.content: The sesame bun contains wheat, making it unsuitable for gluten‑free diets.

items.title: Processed meat additives
items.content: The patty may contain preservatives and additives that should be limited in a healthy diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burger is served hot and can be eaten straight away. Add extra sauce, onions or lettuce if desired. For a lighter option, swap the regular bun for a whole‑grain version.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Consume the prepared burger within 2 hours at room temperature. If you need to store it, refrigerate at 4 °C and eat within 24 hours. Reheat on a grill or in a microwave before serving.
